Then grep the tree for a committed fixture declaring `cur` (not `pkgCur`) at package level: none. | cp tests/b1-lines-r2-addr-nonrealm-cur.gno gnovm/tests/files/zrealm_cur_addr_int.gno && go test ./gnovm/pkg/gnolang/ -run 'TestFiles/zrealm_cur_addr_int.gno$'
verdicts.tldr: no write spelling escapes the three guards today, and the misleading `&cur` message needs source the type checker already rejects at both shas
verdicts.details: The structural half reads true: preprocess.go:2583, 3011 and 3116 each ask isCrossingCurParam (preprocess.go:6111) the same declaring-block question, ~31 lines of rule across four places, and no rewrite was shipped to price against it. But the loss it claims never materialises: rerunning the finder's own sweep at head refuses both extra write spellings, and the address-of arm needs a non-realm binding spelled `cur` inside a crossing function's own block, which cannot type-check at either sha because the first realm parameter is `cur` by rule (preprocess.go:2828) or `.arg` for a blank, which the type checker itself names `cur`. What survives is narrower than the candidate: the package-level arm of fix 2 changed behaviour (base panics on `cur = r`, head accepts) and no committed fixture covers it, since zrealm_cur_other_legal.gno spells that arm `pkgCur`. Fix: none for the enumeration; the one real gap is a fixture declaring a package-level `var cur realm`, which belongs to the missing-test candidate rather than this refactor.
verdicts.evidence: sh tests/b1-refactor-r2-write-shape-sweep.sh at 6d88deba7: `zzz_b1_var_cur_decl.gno:7:6: cur redeclared in this block` and `zzz_b1_decompose_cur.gno:10:2-19: cannot reassign the crossing `cur` parameter` -- both spellings refused. My own probe (judge-32), `func main(_ realm) { var cur int = 42; println(cur) }`, at 6d88deba7 AND at b7845fb2d, byte-identical output: `zrealm_cur_nonrealm_probe.gno:5:6: cur redeclared in this block; ...:4:19: other declaration of cur` -- the finder's zrealm_cur_addr_int.gno only reached preprocess at head because the filetest harness surfaced the panic before the same type-check diff. Package-level arm, b1-reach-r2-pkglevel-cur-untested.gno: head `ok github.com/gnolang/gno/gnovm/pkg/gnolang 0.042s`, base `unexpected panic: zrealm_cur_pkglevel_probe.gno:36:2-9: cannot reassign the crossing `cur` parameter`; grep of gnovm/tests/files for a package-level `cur` returns only zrealm_cur_other_legal.gno, which declares `var pkgCur realm`.
verdicts.refuted_by: preprocess.go:2828 `panic("a crossing function's first realm argument must have name `cur`")`, and the type checker at both shas: `cur redeclared in this block; ... other declaration of cur`
